title: Compare and Contrast Methods for Optimizing Workloads Using Cloud Resources

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Cloud optimization means matching the workload to the resources that serve it.
You do not automatically throw a virtual machine at everything.
CompTIA wants you to recognize how compute, orchestration, workflows, networking, storage performance, and managed services affect workload efficiency.

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: What is actually limiting or complicating this workload: compute model, coordination, process flow, network performance, storage performance, or administration?
sections.callout: Identify the bottleneck or workload requirement first → then choose the cloud resource.

entries.title: Virtual Machine (VM)
paragraphs: A virtual machine provides a complete virtual machine environment including an operating system.
Virtual machines provide strong isolation and flexibility for applications that need their own operating system environment.
Think: I need the whole virtual computer.
entries.recognitionCue: If the workload needs a complete isolated operating system environment → think virtual machine.

entries.title: Container
paragraphs: A container packages an application and its dependencies without requiring the same full guest operating system footprint as a virtual machine.
Containers are useful for portable, modular workloads.
Think: Package the application, not an entire computer.
entries.recognitionCue: If the workload needs lightweight portable application packaging → think container.

entries.title: Serverless
paragraphs: Serverless computing lets a developer run workloads without managing the underlying servers directly.
The cloud provider handles much of the infrastructure operation.
Think: Run the workload; don't manage the server.
entries.recognitionCue: If the organization wants code or workloads to run without server administration → think serverless.

sections.title: Orchestration
paragraphs: Orchestration coordinates multiple cloud resources or workloads so they operate together.
Instead of manually managing each component, orchestration automates their coordination.
Think: Coordinate the whole orchestra.
sections.callout: If many resources must be automatically coordinated → think orchestration.

sections.title: Workflow
paragraphs: A workflow defines the sequence of steps required to complete a process.
One activity may trigger another until the job finishes.
Think: Step A → Step B → Step C.
Workflow describes what steps happen and in what order. Orchestration coordinates the systems or resources that perform the work.
sections.callout: If the scenario describes an ordered sequence of tasks → think workflow.

entries.title: Latency
paragraphs: Latency measures delay. It is how long it takes for traffic to travel and receive a response.
Think: How long did the trip take?
Applications that require immediate interaction can suffer when latency is high.
entries.recognitionCue: If users complain about delay or response time → think network latency.

entries.title: Throughput
paragraphs: Network throughput measures the amount of data successfully transferred over time.
Think: How much can move through the pipe?
A network may have acceptable latency but insufficient throughput for transferring large amounts of data.
entries.recognitionCue: If the issue is the volume of data transferred over time → think network throughput.

sections.title: Storage

entries.title: Input/Output Operations per Second (IOPS)
paragraphs: Input/output operations per second measures how many storage input/output operations can occur within a second.
Workloads performing large numbers of storage operations may require high IOPS.
Think: How many storage jobs can happen each second?
entries.recognitionCue: If the application performs many small or frequent disk operations → think IOPS.

entries.title: Throughput
paragraphs: Storage throughput measures how much storage data can be transferred over time.
Large sequential transfers may care heavily about throughput.
Think: How much storage data can move through the pipe?
entries.recognitionCue: If the workload moves large amounts of storage data → think storage throughput.

sections.callout: IOPS = number of operations. Storage throughput = amount of data.

sections.title: Managed Services
paragraphs: Using managed services can optimize operations by shifting more infrastructure administration to the cloud provider.
This can reduce the effort required to maintain supporting systems.
Think: Do we need to operate this ourselves, or can the provider do it?
sections.callout: If reducing infrastructure-management overhead is the optimization goal → think managed service.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Complete operating system environment → Virtual machine
Run workload without managing server → Serverless
Network delay or response time → Latency
Network data transferred over time → Network throughput
Amount of storage data transferred → Storage throughput

entries.title: Virtual Machine vs. Container vs. Serverless
paragraphs: Do not choose based only on the fact that all three can run applications. Ask how much environment the workload actually needs.
A full machine environment points to a virtual machine. A packaged application points to a container. A workload without server management points to serverless.

entries.title: Latency vs. Throughput
paragraphs: Fast response is not the same as moving lots of data. Delay points to latency; volume over time points to throughput.

entries.title: IOPS vs. Storage Throughput
paragraphs: A workload performing thousands of small operations may need high IOPS. A workload transferring large amounts of data may need high throughput.

entries.title: Orchestration vs. Workflow
paragraphs: Workflow describes sequence. Orchestration describes coordination.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
bullets: Need complete virtual operating system → Virtual machine
Do not want to manage servers → Serverless
Need more network data transferred per second → Network throughput
Need more storage operations per second → IOPS
Need more storage data transferred per second → Storage throughput
